description: A coalition of mid-sized EU member states, frustrated by the paralysis of central decision-making, begins informal coordination with Japan, South Korea, and Canada on joint AI safety testing and compute procurement, bypassing both Brussels and Washington. This shadow framework emerges from existing research ties and shared frustration over access and sovereignty. It is not yet formalised, but early data-sharing and joint red-teaming exercises are underway.

A grassroots movement of municipal governments and regional energy providers begins retrofitting decommissioned industrial sites into community-owned AI training facilities, powered by surplus renewable energy. The first cluster goes live in Spain and Finland, attracting technical volunteers and small-scale research collectives. Though individually small, the network signals a bottom-up alternative to state- or corporate-controlled compute, and begins drawing policy interest as a resilience experiment.
